content: Your doctor has prescribed famotidine to reduce the amount of acid produced by your stomach. This medication is used to treat and prevent ulcers and to manage other conditions where excessive stomach acid is a problem. Famotidine will be administered either by adding it to an intravenous fluid that drips through a needle or catheter placed in your vein for at least 15 minutes, once or twice daily, or by continuous infusion over 24 hours. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Your healthcare provider may monitor the effectiveness and side effects of your treatment through laboratory tests and physical examinations. It is crucial to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and the laboratory. The duration of your treatment will depend on how well you respond to the medication. Before receiving famotidine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to famotidine, cimetidine (Tagamet), nizatidine (Axid), ranitidine (Zantac), or any other medications. Additionally, provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking famotidine, contact your doctor immediately. Before administering famotidine, carefully inspect the solution. It should be clear and free of any floating particles. Gently squeeze the bag or examine the container to ensure there are no leaks. Do not use the solution if it is discolored, contains particles, or if the bag or container is leaking. Use a new solution, but show the damaged one to your healthcare provider. It is essential to use your medication exactly as directed. Do not alter your dosing schedule without consulting your healthcare provider. If you experience a mechanical problem, such as a blockage in the tubing, needle, or catheter, your healthcare provider may instruct you to stop the infusion. If this occurs, contact your healthcare provider immediately to ensure your therapy continues without interruption. Famotidine may cause side effects. Notify your healthcare provider if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: headache, dizziness, constipation, or diarrhea. If you are receiving famotidine intravenously, your healthcare provider will likely provide you with a supply of the medication and instruct you to store it in the refrigerator or freezer. Take your next dose out of the refrigerator one hour before use and place it in a clean, dry area to allow it to reach room temperature. If you are instructed to store additional famotidine in the freezer, transfer a 24-hour supply to the refrigerator for the next day’s use. Do not refreeze the medication. Store your medication only as directed and ensure you understand the proper storage requirements. Keep your supplies in a clean, dry place when not in use, and store all medications and supplies out of reach of children. Your healthcare provider will explain how to safely dispose of used needles, syringes, tubing, and containers to prevent accidental injury. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. If you are receiving famotidine intravenously or subcutaneously, it is important to recognize the symptoms of a catheter-related infection, which can occur at the site where the needle enters your vein or skin.
